hints: Write Newton's second law horizontally for particle $A$ ($0.3\text{ kg}$ on smooth table): $T = 0.3a$.
Write Newton's second law down the incline for particle $B$ ($0.5\text{ kg}$ on smooth $30^\circ$ slope): $3.5 + 0.5g\sin 30^\circ - T = 0.5a$.
Add the equations to find $a$, then substitute back to find tension $T$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law horizontally to particle $A$ ($m_A = 0.3\text{ kg}$):
$$T = 0.3a \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Apply Newton's second law down the plane to particle $B$ ($m_B = 0.5\text{ kg}$) with $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$3.5 + 0.5g\sin 30^\circ - T = 0.5a$$
$$3.5 + 0.5(10)(0.5) - T = 0.5a$$
$$3.5 + 2.5 - T = 0.5a$$
$$6 - T = 0.5a \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Add Equation 1 and Equation 2 to eliminate $T$:
$$6 = 0.3a + 0.5a = 0.8a$$
$$a = \frac{6}{0.8} = 7.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = 7.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into Equation 1 to find $T$:
$$T = 0.3(7.5) = 2.25\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Connected-Particle Systems: Sets up $T = 0.3a$ and $3.5 + 2.5 - T = 0.5a$, solves to find $a = 7.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $T = 2.25\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough: Consider the two particles connected by the string. Both have the same acceleration magnitude $a$ along the line of motion.

Isolate particle $A$ on the smooth horizontal plane:
The only horizontal force acting on $A$ is the tension $T$ towards the pulley:
$$T = m_A a = 0.3a \quad \text{(Equation 1)}$$

Isolate particle $B$ on the smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$:
Forces acting parallel to the incline down the slope are:
1. The applied force: $3.5\text{ N}$.
2. The component of weight: $m_B g\sin 30^\circ = 0.5 \times 10 \times 0.5 = 2.5\text{ N}$.
The force acting up the slope is the tension $T$.
Apply Newton's second law down the plane:
$$3.5 + m_B g\sin 30^\circ - T = m_B a$$
$$3.5 + 2.5 - T = 0.5a$$
$$6 - T = 0.5a \quad \text{(Equation 2)}$$

Add Equation 1 and Equation 2 to eliminate $T$:
$$(6 - T) + T = 0.5a + 0.3a$$
$$6 = 0.8a$$
Divide by $0.8$:
$$a = \frac{6}{0.8} = 7.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = 7.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into Equation 1:
$$T = 0.3 \times 7.5 = 2.25\text{ N}$$

hints: Calculate the loss in gravitational potential energy of $B$ as it descends $0.6\text{ m}$ along the $30^\circ$ incline: $\Delta E_p = 0.5g(0.6\sin 30^\circ)$.
Calculate the work done by the applied force: $3.5 \times 0.6\text{ J}$.
Write the work-energy balance for the two-particle system: Work by applied force + PE loss = Gain in KE of both particles + Work done against friction.
walkthrough:
Calculate the gravitational potential energy lost by particle $B$ over distance $s = 0.6\text{ m}$ down the $30^\circ$ slope:
$$\Delta E_{p, B} = m_B g(s\sin 30^\circ) = 0.5(10)(0.6 \times 0.5) = 1.5\text{ J}$$

Calculate the work done by the applied $3.5\text{ N}$ force over $0.6\text{ m}$:
$$W_{\text{applied}} = 3.5 \times 0.6 = 2.1\text{ J}$$

Apply the work-energy principle to the connected system of total mass $m_{\text{total}} = 0.3 + 0.5 = 0.8\text{ kg}$ starting from rest:
$$W_{\text{applied}} + \Delta E_{p, B} = \frac{1}{2} m_{\text{total}} v^2 + W_{\text{friction}}$$
$$2.1 + 1.5 = \frac{1}{2}(0.8) v^2 + 1.1$$
$$3.6 = 0.4 v^2 + 1.1$$

ai_rubric.Applying the Work–Energy Principle: Calculates PE loss $= 1.5\text{ J}$, WD by applied force $= 2.1\text{ J}$, forms $2.1 + 1.5 = \frac{1}{2}(0.8)v^2 + 1.1$, and finds $v = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

teacher_walkthrough: Use an energy method for the whole system consisting of particles $A$ ($0.3\text{ kg}$) and $B$ ($0.5\text{ kg}$). Both particles move a distance $d = 0.6\text{ m}$ from rest and acquire the same final speed $v$.

1. Work done by the applied force of $3.5\text{ N}$:
$$W_{\text{applied}} = F \times d = 3.5 \times 0.6 = 2.1\text{ J}$$

2. Potential energy change:
Particle $A$ moves horizontally, so its potential energy is unchanged ($\Delta E_{p, A} = 0$).
Particle $B$ descends along the $30^\circ$ incline, losing vertical height:
$$h = d\sin 30^\circ = 0.6 \times 0.5 = 0.3\text{ m}$$
$$\Delta E_{p, \text{loss}} = m_B g h = 0.5 \times 10 \times 0.3 = 1.5\text{ J}$$

3. Total kinetic energy gained by both particles from rest:
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}(m_A + m_B)v^2 = \frac{1}{2}(0.3 + 0.5)v^2 = \frac{1}{2}(0.8)v^2 = 0.4 v^2$$
4. Work done against friction is given directly as $W_{\text{friction}} = 1.1\text{ J}$.

State the work-energy balance equation for the system:
$$\text{Energy input} = \text{Energy output}$$
$$W_{\text{applied}} + \Delta E_{p, \text{loss}} = \Delta E_k + W_{\text{friction}}$$
Substitute the calculated values:
$$2.1 + 1.5 = 0.4 v^2 + 1.1$$
$$3.6 = 0.4 v^2 + 1.1$$
Subtract $1.1$ from both sides:
$$0.4 v^2 = 2.5$$
Divide by $0.4$:
$$v^2 = \frac{2.5}{0.4} = \frac{25}{4} = 6.25$$
Take the square root:
$$v = \sqrt{6.25} = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
